issues.sym: Knocking or rattling from the engine, rough running, stalling, a check engine or oil warning, and in the worst case the engine failing while you drive. A failed bearing can break through the block and spill hot oil, which is a fire risk.
issues.why: Some bearings inside the variable-compression turbo engine were made with flaws and can wear out. NHTSA campaign 25V-437 covers the 2022 QX55 along with other Nissan and Infiniti models that use this engine. One owner reported stalling and white smoke, and the dealer found metal shavings and said the engine needed replacing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall now. The dealer updates the engine computer software and inspects the engine, and replaces it if damage is found. If you hear knocking or the oil light comes on, pull over safely, shut the engine off and have it towed.

issues.t: Engine knocking and power loss from bearing damage
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, grinding or knocking from the engine, and the oil and check engine lights coming on. The car may become undrivable.
issues.why: A 2023 QX55 owner reported a connecting rod bearing failure at about 16,500 miles, with metal debris found in the turbocharger oil line, so the engine and turbo had to be replaced. The 2023 model is not part of the 2022 bearing recall.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as it is safe if you hear knocking or see the oil light; running it longer destroys the engine. Have it towed to a dealer, keep your oil change records, and ask for warranty coverage. The powertrain warranty should still cover most 2023 models.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates for no reason
issues.sym: The car brakes hard or flashes a collision warning with a loud beep when nothing is in the way, for example when driving into a shadow.
issues.why: The forward radar and camera can wrongly detect an obstacle. A 2022 QX55 owner reported the system braking unexpectedly at about 21,600 miles and the car feeling hard to control for several seconds.
issues.next: Hold the wheel firmly and keep driving straight if it happens. Report it to the dealer and to NHTSA, and ask the dealer to check for sensor and software updates and to recalibrate the radar. Keep the front sensor area clean.

issues.t: Driver-assist warning from radar fault code
issues.sym: A warning that the emergency braking, cruise control or other driver-assist features are unavailable, sometimes coming and going.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB21-025 covers QX55s that store code C1A17 in the front radar sensor, which switches off the radar-based safety systems.
issues.next: Clean any snow, mud or bugs off the front grille area where the sensor sits. If the warning stays on, have the dealer apply the bulletin. Drive without relying on the assist features until it is fixed.

issues.t: Roaring cooling fan and weak A/C
issues.sym: A loud roaring or droning from the front of the car with the engine running, and the A/C blowing warm or not cooling well.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletins ITB22-025 and ITB22-025B address a noisy engine cooling fan assembly that can also leave the A/C struggling.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. Ask the dealer to check the cooling fan under the bulletin, which may be covered by warranty.

issues.t: Rear differential noise, vibration or binding
issues.sym: A whine, groan or shudder from the rear of the car, or a binding feeling in tight turns.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB12-072 (revision I) lists the QX55 for abnormal noise, vibration or binding from the rear differential on all-wheel-drive models. Every US QX55 has all-wheel drive.
issues.next: Have the dealer road-test the car and check the differential fluid. The bulletin usually calls for a fluid change or repair, and it may be covered under warranty.

issues.t: Fuel or oil smell in a closed garage
issues.sym: A gasoline or oily smell in the garage after you park the car.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB21-020 covers fuel or oil odors from parked QX55s in enclosed garages.
issues.next: Look under the car for drips. If there is a wet fuel leak, do not drive it and call the dealer. Otherwise ask the dealer to apply the bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P11A7
issues.sym: Check engine light on, usually with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB21-027 addresses the check engine light coming on with code P11A7 stored in the engine computer on the QX55.
issues.next: Have the code read. If P11A7 is stored, ask the dealer to apply the bulletin; this is usually a warranty repair.

issues.sym: The clock on the screen or dash drifts or shows the wrong time.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB21-026 provides a software update for an incorrect clock on the QX55.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the software update at your next visit. It is a nuisance, not a safety problem.

issues.t: Apple CarPlay or Bluetooth keeps disconnecting
issues.sym: The phone drops off Bluetooth or CarPlay a few minutes into a drive, the screen freezes or reboots, or the audio system acts up.
issues.why: A 2023 owner reported CarPlay and Bluetooth disconnecting on every drive for two years without a dealer fix. Infiniti has issued infotainment bulletins for the QX55, including AV control unit information (ITB19-030) and updates for frequent reboots (ITB23-009/ITB23-010).
issues.next: Update your phone, delete and re-pair it, and try a different cable. Ask the dealer to install the latest infotainment software.

issues.t: Front passenger door may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: The front passenger door stays unlocked when the others lock. In a crash an unlocked door is more likely to open.
issues.why: Some 2023 QX55s got the wrong latch in the right front door lock assembly. NHTSA campaign 23V-187 covers it (Nissan number PC962).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the passenger door lock assembly for free.

issues.t: Check engine light from EVAP vent valve (P0448)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0448 and no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB22-042 covers the check engine light for the fuel vapor (EVAP) vent control valve on the QX55.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel cap or filler is closed properly. If the light stays on, ask the dealer to apply the bulletin. It is not urgent, but it can fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Grease leaking from drive shaft boot
issues.sym: Dark grease splattered inside the wheel well or on suspension parts near a wheel.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB22-041 covers grease leaking from a drive shaft (CV) boot on the QX55.
issues.next: Have it looked at soon. A boot leaking grease lets dirt into the joint, and a worn joint clicks when turning and eventually needs replacing. Ask about warranty coverage.

issues.t: Rear seat heater overheats and scorches the cushion
issues.sym: A hot or burning smell from the back seat, and stains or scorch marks on the rear seat cushion.
issues.why: A 2023 owner reported the rear seat heater overheating and burning the seat cushions. The heating element or its control can fail and stay on too hot.
issues.next: Switch off the rear seat heaters and do not use them until checked, since overheating is a burn and fire risk. Report it to the dealer and to NHTSA, and push for warranty repair.

issues.t: Tire sidewall may be cut from the factory (service campaign)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice until a tire goes flat or bulges. A cut in the sidewall can lead to a sudden air loss.
issues.why: Infiniti campaign PC911 inspected certain 2022-2023 QX models for cuts in the outer tire sidewall made during production. A similar quality action (IPSB 15-286) inspects the inner sidewall on 2025 QX50s and QX55s.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether your VIN is in a tire campaign. Look over all four sidewalls, and replace any tire with a cut, bulge or exposed cords before driving at speed.

issues.sym: The engine stalls, hesitates or picks up speed very slowly.
issues.why: Owners report stalling and slow acceleration on the QX55, and RepairPal says it is often traced to a failing fuel pump.
issues.next: If it stalls in traffic, turn on your hazard lights and get off the road. Have the fuel pressure and codes checked; the fuel pump should be covered if the car is still under warranty.

issues.sym: The car will not start, clicks, or the battery is dead after sitting.
issues.why: RepairPal lists starter problems and dead batteries among reported QX55 problems.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested first. If the battery tests fine but the car still clicks, the starter may need replacing.
